description:
151.83 km/h. The fastest speed ever recorded on a skateboard. 
Prada Linea Rossa joins Red Bull athlete and two-time downhill world champion Diego Poncelet in the Skateboard Speed World Record project, supporting his pursuit of a historic milestone. 
On a closed section of Route des Éboulements in Québec, Canada, Poncelet surpasses the previous world record following years of research, training, and technical development. 
Working closely with the athlete, Prada Linea Rossa developed bespoke footwear and gloves, combining high-performance materials with protection, comfort, and grip. Every detail contributed to a system engineered for control at extreme speeds. 
A new chapter in the ongoing partnership between Prada Linea Rossa and Red Bull, challenging conventions and redefining the boundaries of human performance.

description:
With Re-Cashmere and Re-Wool, Prada extends the circular approach first articulated through Re-Nylon into the register of natural fibre, translating a commitment to lower-impact responsible material sourcing into two of fashion’s most storied materials: wool and cashmere. 

Here, circularity begins upstream, at the moment of making: pre-consumer offcuts, spinning residues and cutting-room remainders are gathered, sorted and recycled into high-quality secondary raw materials that return to the production cycle. 

Behind each garment stands a network of specialised suppliers, bound together in close collaboration across every stage of the process. Re-Cashmere and Re-Wool are made entirely in Italy, in Tuscany and Umbria, where knitwear craftmanship finds its truest expression.

description:
Pradasphere unfolds across the piano nobile of Prada Galleria as the first permanent exhibition dedicated to Prada, tracing more than a century of creativity from the 1913 founding of Fratelli Prada to the present day. 
Gathering artifacts from the archive and decades of engagement across art, architecture, film, culture, and sport, many on view for the first time, the exhibition offers a living record of the brand’s evolution over the past century. 
Pradasphere follows the success of earlier traveling iterations in London and Hong Kong in 2014, and Shanghai in 2023, returning the story to Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the historic home of Fratelli Prada.

Emilia Clarke at the Prada Spring/Summer 2027 Womenswear Fashion Show in Milan. 
She reflects on “The Skirt”, the Prada Spring/Summer 2027 Womenswear Collection by Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons. 
Engineered for freedom, the skirt is a Prada obsession. At once autonomous and interdependent of the clothes around, its definitive graphic silhouette, linear and modernist, offers the single fixed parameter for projection of ideas. The collection stays within the particular form language of this specific skirt, as an exercise of exploration inside strict parameters, a frame for ceaseless creation.

“The Skirt”, the Prada Spring/Summer 2027 Womenswear Fashion Show by Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons. 
Purpose and use form an aesthetic language distinct to Prada. Materialities directly transform perception, challenging and subverting established form language. 
Our perception of a garment may be changed through its friction with other. A skirt may be abstracted, a fragment of a whole with a mutating rapport with the pieces it juxtaposes: a sweater, a shirt, a bra top, can each suggest alternate readings of a whole. 
Here, there is inherent beauty found in the survey of the familiar - in asking how many forms a known thing might assume, how many different possibilities may exist within.

description:
Precision, concentration, the reactive act. The Spring/Summer 2027 menswear collection by
Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons is built around the notion of choice, of conscious decision.
Rather than reduction, the focus is a distillation, to the fundamental, intentional and
meaningful.
Clothes as universal articles of life, resilient, are reconsidered with new thought.
Rematerialization and reiteration can radically reclassify garment typologies, shifting our viewpoint, their value systems and therefore their quiescent meanings.
Proposed is an exact and highly-controlled silhouette, refined and linear, constant.
Within, a specific lexicon of garments – jeans, jean-jackets, t-shirts, striking in their pragmatic
simplicity – are entirely reevaluated. Freed from extraneous detail and exaggeration, they are offered as a framework for ceaseless possibility and reinterpretation. Accessories are integrated within these overall structures, streamlined to become part of a whole, while paradigmatic clothing styles are reworked, reanalyzed. Pieces that resist time, these clothes defy easy classification of function or era.

#PradaSS27 #MiucciaPrada #RafSimons #Prada

description:
Axiom Space and Prada unveiled the Liquid Cooling and Ventilation Garment (LCVG) designed to be worn by astronauts inside the Axiom Extravehicular Mobility Unit (AxEMU) spacesuit.  
Engineered as the high-performance inner layer of the AxEMU, the LCVG is built to protect astronauts from the unforgiving environment of space, when they explore the lunar surface for the first time in more than 50 years. 
The LCVG collaboration draws on Prada's expertise in design, patternmaking, and advanced materials, resulting in a next-generation garment developed through advanced 3D modeling techniques that maintain cooling and ventilation while enhancing comfort during up to eight-hour spacewalks.  
Prada's firmly established knowledge of high-performance materials has also supported the identification and sourcing of specialized fibers that allow the garment to be worn repeatedly and comfortably across long-duration missions.

Prada limited-edition collection of sandals combines traditional techniques with Prada’s contemporary design and premium materials to create a unique dialogue between Indian heritage and modern luxury expression. The collection has been manufactured in India by skilled artisans from the Maharashtra and Karnataka regions.​

As a part of the project, the Group is pleased to announce the foundation of a training program fully funded by Prada, including through the proceeds of the sale of the limited-edition sandal collection, dedicated to artisans from the eight districts in India where Kolhapuri Chappals are traditionally manufactured.​

Developed in collaboration with LIDCOM, LIDKAR and leading design institutes - the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT) and the Karnataka Institute of Leather & Fashion Technology (KILT) -, the program is designed to strengthen design and technical skills, enabling artisans to create products that meet evolving market needs, while ensuring the continued relevance of this traditional craft.​

This initiative reflects the Group’s long-standing commitment to reinvest in education and culture.

description:
The conversation continues for Spring/Summer 2026 with American artist Jordan Wolfson, shifting focus from the construction of the image to the construction of the self. The Prada Spring/Summer 2026 collection is reconsidered through a second iteration, where familiar faces are placed in unfamiliar contexts.
Tuba Avalon addresses the work featuring Prada Ambassadors Hunter Schafer, Nicholas Hoult, Damson Idris, Carey Mulligan, with John Glacier, Levon Hawke and Liu Wen. The cast sits alone, encountering imagined creatures: playful, undefined, and not fully explainable.
Repeating a single phrase, “I, I, I, I am…”, the work becomes an open statement, an attempt to define identity that never concludes. Meaning remains unresolved, shaped through repetition, perception, and presence.
Between reality and imagination, identity shifts, disappears, and reappears. The work does not offer answers but opens questions - exploring how we perform, how we are seen, and how we understand ourselves.

description:
For Spring/Summer 2026, Prada starts from something very direct: how clothes feel on the body in uncertain times. The focus is physical ease and movement: garments designed to shift and respond, never fixed or restrictive.

Tuba Avalon considers how this thinking extends into the Spring/Summer 2026 campaign by Anne Collier, featuring Prada Ambassadors Hunter Schafer, Nicholas Hoult, Damson Idris and Carey Mulligan, together with John Glacier, Levon Hawke and Liu Wen. Images do not simply show clothes but translate the ideas behind them.

Anne Collier’s intervention renders the Prada Spring/Summer 2026 campaign as a physical, material object, one to be held, and felt. In each still-life composition, outside hands hold aloft specially-shot imagery of the collection, photographed by Oliver Hadlee Pearch. Like an additional observer, or a reflection of ourselves as onlookers, these images are observed, admired, perhaps desired - examining the mechanism of advertising as a medium.

description:
Prada celebrates the 25th anniversary of the Broadway Epicenter. 
Located at the corner of Prince and Broadway in New York City, the first Prada Epicenter opened to public on December 15, 2001. Conceived in collaboration with Rem Koolhaas and the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA), it was envisioned as a laboratory - an experimental space to explore new forms of retail, customer interaction, and cultural engagement. 
Marking this anniversary, Prada has dedicated its wallpaper installation to celebrate OMA/AMO project designs, featuring diagrams, and imagery generated during the original 2001 collaboration. 
Since its inception, the Broadway Epicenter has functioned as a space defined by transformation.
title: 25 Years of the Prada Broadway Epicenter

“Image of an Image”, the Prada Spring/Summer 2026 campaign, featuring Prada Ambassadors Hunter Schafer, Nicholas Hoult, Damson Idris and Carey Mulligan, together with John Glacier, Levon Hawke and Liu Wen.
A perspective on Prada. Re-considering the Spring/Summer 2026 collections by Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons, the campaign investigates the nature of advertising itself: the image, the medium, the message.

Both a celebration of fashion imagery and a liberation from it, the campaign frames fashion through fine art, reflecting Prada’s long-held exchange with contemporary artists and global culture.

You’ll learn of Dionysus and the maiden Amethyst, and how spilled wine birthed the violet stone. The result is a redefinition of preciousness: liberated, radiant, alive with unexpected hues.

The silhouette - sculpted bust, cinched waist, softened hips - emerges through a complex process of pattern making and tailoring. Pleats are layered with double inserts in contrasting fabrics, raw edges are frayed using tailoring scissors and abrasive brushes, and surfaces are pressed to the millimeter before roundness is restored with heat.
Over 24 hours of craftsmanship converge in a final gesture: a two-toned ribbon, hand-tied through raw-edged buttonholes. Each detail becomes a mark of intention. This is where refinement begins at the raw.

Prada Mode Osaka 2025 showcases  Kazuyo Sejima’s transformational projects for the island of Inujima, where art, architecture, and fashion converge in a stunning exhibition at Umekita Park, Osaka. Explore how Prada Mode Osaka celebrates artistic vision in the heart of Umekita Park, Japan, and discover the enduring legacy of the Inujima Art House Project. title: Infrastructure and Ecology | The Final Day of Prada Frames in Milan

description:
Embark on a reflective journey through Prada Frames 2025, the three-day symposium curated by design and research studio Formafantasma. Set aboard the Arlecchino train as well as in the Padiglione Reale, “In Transit” investigates infrastructure as a force shaping movement, society, and the built environment through cross-disciplinary dialogue.
Prada Frames embodies the brand’s commitment to intellectual exploration and aesthetic inquiry. Conceived as a cultural laboratory, the symposium convenes influential thinkers across disciplines - spanning architecture, art, philosophy, and science - to interrogate the systems that shape contemporary life. In its 2025 edition, In Transit addresses the infrastructure of movement in all its material and immaterial forms, from planetary networks to ecological shifts.

Moderated by Alice Rawsthorn, the symposium included contributions from Kate Crawford, Marina Otero Verzier, Jesse LeCavalier, Rose George, Samia Henni, Hito Steyerl, Charlotte Malterre-Barthes, AAU Anastas, Marta Foresti, Lorenzo Pezzani, Nelly Ben Hayoun-Stépanian, Giacomo Abbruzzese, Metahaven, Tung-Hui Hu, Julia Watson, Nick Hunt, Ersilia Vaudo, Nicola Twilley, and Paola Antonelli, in conversation with Natalia Grabowska.

#Prada #PradaFrames

Discover more about Prada Frames here: https://tinyurl.com/43j97um8

description:
A luminous interplay of light and craftsmanship—this is Made in Prada: Reflections of Craft. Witness the meticulous making of a Prada Spring/Summer 2025 dress, where tradition and innovation converge.​

Beginning with nearly weightless tulle embroidery, the piece is adorned with a stream of silver sequins applied using Prada embroidery techniques. A second layer, completed by hand, brings mirror embellishment and crystal embroidery into a carefully orchestrated composition. Each mirror, framed by faceted stones, creates a three-dimensional play of reflections, embodying Prada savoir faire.​

Every step in this fashion embroidery process is a testament to skill, patience, and artistic precision. The garment, after 3 days of expert craftsmanship, takes its final shape—an expression of light sculpted onto fabric.​

description:
In the final chapter of the Prada Re-Nylon film series, Prada Ambassador Sadie Sink journeys to the Great Kelp Highway of Northern and Central America with National Geographic CreativeWorks. Exploring the fragile balance of this marine ecosystem, she uncovers the impact of overfishing and pollution on the once-thriving kelp forests.
Guided by marine biologist, SEA BEYONDer and Goodwill Ambassador of the project Giovanni Chimienti and scientist Rodrigo Beas, she delves into the biodiversity of these underwater forests - home to edible fish, shellfish, marine mammals, and seabirds. The episode highlights the urgency of protecting these delicate habitats through knowledge and action.
Through the SEA BEYOND initiative, a partnership between Prada Group and UNESCO-IOC, Prada sustainability efforts continue to inspire younger generations in ocean education. 

1% of the proceeds from the Prada Re-Nylon for SEA BEYOND Collection benefit the SEA BEYOND project by Prada Group and in partnership with UNESCO-IOC.

description:
Prada presented the eleventh iteration of Prada Mode at MiZa, in Mina Zayed, Abu Dhabi.
This edition marked Prada’s latest collaboration and third iteration of Prada Mode with multidisciplinary artist Theaster Gates. The event reaffirmed themes of minimalism and analogue aesthetics amidst contemporary digital culture, featuring an architectural intervention that divided the space into two distinct sonic and tonal realms.
The cultural programming, curated by Myrna Ayad, showcased local and regional talent, emphasizing the intelligence, creativity, and contributions of Arab women. Across two days, guests engaged in discussions such as “Honoring Tradition, Celebrating Modernity” and “The Power of the Matriarch”, alongside interactive Al-Sadu weaving workshops—a UNESCO-recognized Bedouin weaving tradition.
Live performances by artists such as Nancy Mounir, musicians of Noura Mint Seymali x Aïta Mon Amour, and DJs Yas Meen Selectress, Nooriyah, and Deena Abdelwahed provided a sonic backdrop to the immersive experience. The event concluded with an exclusive celebration honoring the intersection of art, culture, and contemporary thought.

description:

Panettone Custard Cream Recipe
Ingredients (for 1 panettone):
• 200 g milk
• 50 g sugar
• 80 g egg yolks
• 15 g rice/corn starch
• 2 vanilla pods

Preparation:
1. In a saucepan, bring the milk and vanilla pods to a boil.
2. Separately, mix the sugar with the egg yolks and sifted starch.
3. Gradually add the boiling milk to the mixture while whisking.
4. Return the mixture to heat and bring to a boil again, stirring continuously.
5. Cool immediately and store in the fridge.

Join Prada Ambassador Karina as she bakes her favorite gingerbread cookies. These spiced cookies come straight from the timeless recipes of Marchesi 1824. They’re perfect for your holiday celebrations. Did you already try this recipe? Share your thoughts in the comments!

The Prada Holiday campaign celebrates the beauty of baking and festive traditions, bringing a touch of refined taste through its collaboration with Marchesi 1824.

#Prada #PradaHoliday #PradaGifts #Karina

Gingerbread Cookies Recipe
Ingredients (for 40 biscuits):
• 460 g icing sugar
• 360 g butter
• 60 g eggs
• 200 g milk
• 8 g baking powder
• 6 g salt
• 12 g ginger powder
• 2 vanilla pods
• 1 kg weak white flour (biscuit flour)

Preparation:
1. Mix the soft butter with the icing sugar and salt. Add the inside of the vanilla pods and mix well.
2. Add the eggs and milk, which have been previously mixed together, and combine well.
3. Add the sifted flour, baking powder, and ginger powder. Mix everything to form a smooth dough.
4. Leave the dough to rest in the fridge, covered with cling film, for at least 4 hours.
5. Roll out the dough to 3 mm thickness and cut into shapes as desired.
6. Bake in a preheated oven at 170°C for 16-18 minutes.
7. Once cooled, decorate with white or colored royal icing.

White Icing:
• 200 g egg whites
• 1000 g powdered sugar
• 5 g lemon juice

Mince Pies Recipe
Ingredients (for 20 pies):

Brisè Pastry:
• 225 g butter
• 450 g flour
• 1 g salt
• 100 ml water

Filling:
• 150 g apples
• 50 g sugar
• 80 g almonds
• 50 g candied orange
• 100 g raisins
• 100 g dried red fruits
• 100 g dried apricots
• 1 g cinnamon powder
• 10 g ginger
• 100 ml brandy
• 60 g melted butter
• 2 g lemon peel

Preparation:
1. Prepare the dough by mixing cold butter with flour and salt. Add water slowly until the dough forms. Let it rest in the fridge for at least 4 hours.
2. For the filling, peel and dice apples. Mix with all the other ingredients and leave to macerate in the fridge overnight.
3. Line small molds with the brisè pastry, fill with the prepared mixture, and decorate with pastry stars.
4. Bake at 180°C for 25 minutes. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

Hot Chocolate Recipe
Ingredients:
• 500 ml milk
• 90 g dark chocolate (68%)
• 25 g icing sugar
• 10 g cornstarch
• 25 g cocoa powder

Whipped Cream Topping:
• 250 g cold fresh cream
• 15 g icing sugar

Preparation:
1. Heat the milk in a saucepan until it reaches 85°C.
2. Separately, mix the sugar, cornstarch, and cocoa powder. Slowly add the hot milk to the dry mixture while stirring continuously.
3. Add the finely chopped dark chocolate and return to the heat. Stir until smooth.
4. Whip the cream with icing sugar and serve the hot chocolate topped with whipped cream.

description:
Join Prada for an in-depth look at the intersection of interior design, environmental sustainability, and contemporary challenges at Prada Frames 2024 symposium, entitled Being Home. This annual multi-day event, curated by the design and research studio Formafantasma, featured contributions from scholars and professionals in diverse research areas, including interior design, sociology, and environmental science. 
Taking place at the historic Bagatti Valsecchi Museum in Milan, the symposium explored the evolving role of the home as a framework for addressing socio-economic norms and environmental concerns. From intimate conversations to thematic lectures, the event offered a unique opportunity to explore the relationship between interior design styles and contemporary challenges.

description:
On May 12 and 13, 2023, Prada presents the ninth iteration of Prada Mode in Tokyo, in association with the Tokyo Metropolitan Government and the Teien Art Museum, one of Japan’s most important cultural properties. 

This unique architectural and cultural journey is hosted and curated by Kazuyo Sejima, the director of Teien Art Museum, architect, and a long-term collaborator of Prada. 

For Prada Mode, the Tokyo Metropolitan Teien Art Museum will be transformed into a space where the guests can explore art in different forms and experience the historic architecture, the museum and the site-specific art works, curated by Kazuyo Sejima, located in the large gardens surrounding the museum. The main temporary pavilion, a wooden curved surface to host conversations, will be placed in the European garden; while various areas will be created spreading along the space for the guests to enjoy the venue as a whole.

description:
During Session 5, electronic waste sites of accumulation were introduced by the speakers, emphasising several models of production and care across the globe. BLANCA CALLÉN shared her current projects on repair techniques. Later, GRACE AKESE introduced the forces shaping e-waste landscapes. BAS VAN ABEL later highlighted the connections between technology and circular economies. The session ended with a conversation between inventor VEENA SAHAJWALLA and design critic ALICE RAWSTHORN on material flows, waste management, and recirculation.

- Blanca Callen, Lecturer and Researcher, University of Vic and Co-founder of Restarters BCN

description:
During Session 3, a series of current works that embrace an expansive attitude toward design was showcased. Firstly, FIONA RABY and ANTHONY DUNNE presented their current research on the entanglement of humans, and objects. The session continued with the presentation of MICHAEL THOMPSON who looked at cityscapes and value systems attached to waste accumulation. Later, entrepreneur LARA GILMORE introduced her social projects working with food waste. Session 3 ended with the discussion between PAOLA ANTONELLI and ALICE RAWSTHORN highlighting examples of attitudinal design practices that recognize the full potential of each citizen to design with tools, beliefs, and care.  

Contributions by:
- Fiona Raby and Anthony Dunne, Principals of Dunne & Raby and University Professors, The New School

description:
During Session 4, material cycles were explored, ranging from space debris with the presentation of RORY HOLMES to digestive systems with the presentation of LYDIA KALLIPOLITI. Later, the fresh graduates of three international higher education spheres (CAROLIN SCHELKLE, EMMIE MASSIAS, ROCIO CROSETTO BRIZZIO and ANA PAOLA HERNANDEZ DERBEZ) introduced some of their projects looking at the potentialities of sand, wool weaving techniques and interspecies alliances. These cycles highlighted the potentialities of rubbish, turd, dirt, and scrap. The session ends with the conversation between SUMAYYA VALLY and NATALIA GRABOWSKA that delved into the complexities of responsible material extraction and application.

description:
Prada presents Asia debut of #PradaFrames - the multidisciplinary symposium conceived by Formafantasma – at M+ in Hong Kong, exploring the complex interaction between design, art and the environment.
The two-day programme, curated by M+, presented an opening lecture by Jacques Herzog, Founding Partner of Herzog & de Meuron.
Discover more: https://tinyurl.com/3zxth6hs 

In his lecture Jacques Herzog told how museums act as containers and circuits for the flow of ideas from the past and look to the future, activated by people.
In addition, the architect explained how the architecture of a museum plays a significant role in shaping and cultivating fundamental and imaginative ideas for a sustainable society.

Introduction: Keri Ryan
Speaker: Jacques Herzog
Interlocutors: Suhanya Raffel and Ikko Yokoyama

Running in parallel to Milan’s Salone del Mobile, Prada Frames is a multidisciplinary symposium that delves into the complex relationship between the natural environment and design. The initiative is a moment of collective reflection that aims at examining and correlating innovative thoughts, while offering a pioneering body of knowledge.Prada Frames is curated by Formafantasma and hosted at the Biblioteca Nazionale Braidense, located in the center of Milan.

00:09 - Introduction
03:56 - URSULA BIEMAN introduced forestal indigenous knowledge and current explorations in the Amazon forest
26:25 - CAVE BUREAU looked at the different meanings the forest has been and continues to be from our ancestral past into our generational future
40:36 - The founders of E-WERK LUCKENWALDE showcase their sustainable sourcing model
01:00:21 - The symposium ended with the discussion between ANNA TSING, FEIFEI ZHOU and ARIC CHEN presenting the work of the Feral Atlas and showing how the attention to phantasmic forms, across scales, brings humans into both the life and death of the forest

description:
Running in parallel to Milan’s Salone del Mobile, Prada Frames is a multidisciplinary symposium that delves into the complex relationship between the natural environment and design. 
The initiative is a moment of collective reflection that aims at examining and correlating innovative thoughts, while offering a pioneering body of knowledge.
Prada Frames is curated by Formafantasma and hosted at the Biblioteca Nazionale Braidense, located in the center of Milan.

0:06 - Introduction
8:45 - SOPHIE CHAO introduced the forest as a living being, Indigenous philosophies of more-than-human coexistence, and drew on modes of reimagining trees and forests as sentient life communities
24:10 - TERESA CASTRO looked into cinematic attempts to engage with more relational modes of perception of the natural environment, introducing the camera as a mediator in the understanding of plants as sentient beings
CASTRO introduced the camera as a mediator in the understanding of plants as sentient beings
46:07 - Conversation between EYAL WEIZMAN and REBECCA LEWIN. The architect explained how architectural tools could also be companions for forensic investigations at the service of ecological and social justice.

Feeling is sensory and emotional—it's about instinct and spontaneity, not intellectual discourse. This campaign is a proposition, a vision of a brand that is intentionally multi-faceted, reflecting its complex and ever-transforming nature. It is that which always Feels Like Prada.

description:
Fusing athleticism, teamwork, and technology, the monohulls competing for the America’s Cup are the fastest in the world. It was August 2012 when the sailing world was turned upside down by a 72-foot catamaran flying in the Hauraki Gulf. Emirates Team New Zealand had brought the foils to the America’s Cup boats and forever changed the face of top-level racing boat competitions. 

Since then, the increase in performance for America’s Cup boats has been greater than at any point in the 170-year history of the event. Six years later, in 2018, the publication of the AC75 Class rule marked the beginning of a new sailing era. Now, foils are commonplace, but the engineering and sailing techniques needed to get the AC75 to fly completely differ from anything seen before.

Martine Syms on creating Chapter 4 of #PradaMultipleViews, the show that never happened: 
"The video is a collage of multiple formats and features iterative, repetitive movements intercut with beautiful people staring at images of themselves on monitors and screens in Milan and in my studio in Los Angeles. Since the collection pieces have a '60s feeling to them, I tried to include several references to cinema culture and surveillance/sousveillance from that time period and the present. I'm inspired by the way screens have come to make and unmake us—and what it means to be living, breathing, moving, fleshy things in a world full of them."

description:
Joanna Piotrowska on creating Chapter 3 of #PradaMultipleViews, the show that never happened: 
"Gesture and physicality are an essential non-verbal form of communication and play a big role in the conceptual and compositional aspects of my work. The finger snap is a quick and subtle, yet attention-demanding action. It is also used to indicate approval or to maintain rhythm. I thought that this short could be an interesting space to work with the snap as a recurring motif that marks the movements and refocuses the viewer’s attention to each new look."

Almost concurrently with the opening of the New York Epicenter, Prada embarked on its second in Tokyo with the Swiss architects Herzog & de Meuron. The six-story stand-alone building, situated in the Aoyama district, is one of the most distinctive works of architecture in Tokyo. 
The green glass façade bulges from a diagonal grid that forms its structural skin. Inside the building houses retail floors, lounges, and event spaces.
Prada Aoyama Tokyo is the first building by Herzog & de Meuron in which the structure, space, and façade form a single unit. The vertical cores, the horizontal tubes, the floor slabs, and the façade grilles define the space but at the same time provide the structure and the façade.

Ca’ Corner della Regina, built between 1724 and 1728 by Domenico Rossi for the Corner family of San Cassiano, is a Venetian palazzo overlooking the Grand Canal and located in the Sestiere of Santa Croce. It was erected on the ruins of the Gothic building in which Caterina Corner, the future queen of Cyprus, was born in 1454. The architecture echoes the style of the nearby Ca’ Pesaro designed by Baldassare Longhena. The frescoes on the first noble floor represent a series of episodes from Caterina Cornaro’s life.

description:
#Prada will present the fourth iteration of Prada Mode, a travelling social club with a focus on contemporary culture that provides members a unique cultural experience along with music, dining, and conversations. Set to align with the opening of Paris Haute Couture on 19–20 January2020, #PradaMode Paris will occupy Maxim’s on 3 Rue Royale,the legendary, 1893 Belle Époque restaurant. A registered national landmark, Maxim’s has welcomed everyone from the artistic andpolitical figures of the early 20th century Parisian world, to the 50s’ Hollywood celebrities, and intelligentsia across all generations.The restaurant’s interiors are a marvel of Art Nouveau design and includes unique masterworks.For Prada Mode Paris, the iconic restaurant will be transformed by AI researcher and professor Kate Crawford and artist and researcher Trevor Paglen — who conceived the Training Humans exhibition onview at Osservatorio Fondazione Prada in Milan until 24 February 2020— into an installation titled “Making Faces” which includes art projectsand architectural modifications focusing on data gathering, surveillanceand facial recognition.

description:
Reflecting changing times and a shifting world, Prada launches a pioneering new project, Re-Nylon, introducing a sustainable line of iconic Prada bag silhouettes executed in a unique new regenerated nylon, ECONYL®.

To showcase the cutting-edge processes behind the Re-Nylon initiative, National Geographic, Prada’s Storytelling Partner, has produced a short video series, What We Carry.

Discover more at https://tinyurl.com/y3of32w6
title: Prada Re-Nylon - Full Episode - What We Carry

description:
The story behind the new #PradaReNylon sustainability initiative has been charted across the globe - uncovering the methods by which harmful and wasteful materials - plastic ocean waste, fishing nets, discarded textiles - are regenerated, revitalised. 
In the final step of this journey through the Re-Nylon project, we are guided by #Prada reporter #AmandaGorman, the inaugural US Youth Poet Laureate whose work celebrates community and social change, and the engineer and architect Arthur Huang, a trailblazer and National Geographic Explorer who focuses on the idea of upcycling waste into new forms. They travelled to Slovenia, a country which has latterly become a hub of a new regenerative and sustainable industry, with 40,000 tons of material recycled annually. It is also home of Aquafil’s production plant for ECONYL®, established in the city of Ljubljana. Alongside Giulio Bonazzi, Chairman and CEO of Aquafil, we are allowed to see some of the intricate chemical recycling process of depolymerisation, used to transforming tons of collected waste into virgin quality, pioneering new ECONYL® yarn.
#PradaGroup
title: Prada Re-Nylon - Episode 5 - What We Carry

description:
For the fourth instalment of the series, National Geographic Explorer and photo journalist Hannah Reyes Morales and Chinese actor and Prada reporter Wei Daxun visit the clothing factory Parawin in Ganzhou City, part of the province of Jiangxi in southeastern China, housing around 300 workers across every part of garment production, from pattern cutting to construction and finishing.

In collaboration with Aquafil, Parawin are now committed to recycling their discarded textile cuttings: offcuts are organised via fiber content and transported regularly to Aquafil’s Shanghai base, to be transformed into ECONYL® regenerated nylon.
title: Prada Re-Nylon - Episode 4 - What We Carry

description:
The third episode in this unfolding five-part series takes us below the surface of the ocean in Mahana Bay, off the coast of New Zealand. It unpacks the ongoing problem of ghosts nets - fishing nets lost or left in the ocean. Around 640,000 tonnes of net are dumped in the ocean each year, which entangle wildlife and have devastating affects on the subterranean ecosystem. 

Australian actor and Prada reporter Alex Fitzalan is joined by National Geographic Explorer, Asha de Vos, a Sri Lankan marine biologist, ocean educator, and pioneer of blue whale research within the northern Indian Ocean as they follow Rob Wilson, co-founder of Ghost Fishing New Zealand and a group of volunteers, removing harmful ghost nets from the sea bed as part of the Healthy Seas initiative, a global non-governmental organization with the aim to remove seas of Marine litter.
title: Prada Re-Nylon - Episode 3 - What We Carry

description:
Reflecting changing times and a shifting world, #Prada launches a pioneering new project, Re-Nylon, introducing a sustainable line of iconic Prada bag silhouettes executed in a unique new regenerated nylon, ECONYL®.
The product of a partnership between Prada and the textile yarn producer Aquafil, ECONYL® nylon is obtained through the recycling and purification process of plastic waste collected from oceans, fishing nets, and textile fibre waste. ECONYL® can be depolymerised, purified, and recycled indefinitely, with no loss of quality.
Re-Nylon is a bold move towards total sustainability - towards an ultimate goal of converting all Prada virgin nylon into regenerated nylon ECONYL® by the end of 2021. It reflects the focus of the #PradaGroup on promoting a corporate culture that aspires to increasingly sustainable balances, incorporating into its daily work the idea of a return of value to society. Re-Nylon is progressive in its concept, forward-looking in its actuality - a leap into the future.
To showcase the cutting-edge processes behind the Re-Nylon initiative, Prada collaborates with National Geographic on a short film series, The Things We Carry.

Discover more at https://tinyurl.com/y3uhwlg2.

#PradaReNylon
title: Prada Re-Nylon - Episode 1 - What We Carry

description:
Inspired by the motion picture universe, for Spring/Summer 2019 Prada unveils its Men’s and Women’s campaigns in synchronicity. Like movie posters, the print campaigns offer windows onto scenes taken from the action.

The premiere instalments are a duo of films showcasing the streamlined modernism of the Spring/Summer 2019 Prada menswear collection, recontextualised by the cinematographic lexicon. Directed by Willy Vanderperre and with Benoît Debie as Director of Photography, the film shorts are enigmatic, a source of fascination, like a tantalizing fragment of a larger whole. A soundscape for each has been scored by Frédéric Sanchez, offering a knowing nod to their Hollywood antecedents.

The films take their stylistic cues from memories of historic moments of the silver screen - rather than indulging cineaphilia, this diptych of shorts are not reiterations of movies past, but reinterpretations arresting in their brevity, offering intriguing glimpses of character.

Each is an examination of the duality central to Prada - two films, offering a second aesthetic interpretation of the Spring/Summer 2019 men’s collection, each showcasing multi-faceted protagonists exploring different sides of themselves.
title: 365, Prada Spring/Summer 2019 Menswear Advertising Campaign - Double Exposure

On October 17, 2017, Prada will open Prada Rong Zhai, a meticulously restored historic early 20th century mansion in central Shanghai. Originally designed for the distinguished family of Yung Tsoong-King*, Rong Zhai is one of Shanghai’s finest Western-style garden villas.

In 2011, Prada began an epic revival of the stunning home, reimaging it as a flexible site for cultural activities. The mansion will not only serve as a unique site for Prada’s diverse activities in China, but also is an emblem of Prada’s admiration of Chinese aesthetic heritage. The history of the mansion can be traced back to 1910. In 1918, Rong Zhai underwent expansion, then became the distinguished family of Yung Tsoong-King’s property. 

While Prada is a luxury fashion brand, we have a longstanding relationship with both radical contemporary architecture and exquisite historic preservation around the world. The restoration of Rong Zhai combines that experience in historic building, an abiding belief in the value of traditional handcraftsmanship, and a dynamic collaboration between Western architects and Chinese scholars and artisans. 

The result is a true hybrid: a dialogue between Milan and Shanghai that stands as a testament to the family that commissioned it, the numerous architects and artists who shaped it, and the teams of Chinese and Italian specialists who brought it back to its rightful grandeur.

Click http://bit.ly/2yaaiWL for more.
title: Unveiling Prada Rong Zhai

Six new Prada realities—Pièce de Chambre, Affiches, Chiaroscuro, Mise-en-Scène, Viewfinder, and Denouement—are unveiled, photographed by Willy Vanderperre. description:
IL PALAZZO, A MULTI-PLATFORM PROJECT COMBINING HAND-MADE ARTISTRY AND CUTTING EDGE TECHNOLOGY

In a sea of documentary fashion photography, Prada takes a new direction collaborating with Richard Haines, a former menswear designer, now fashion illustrator and blogger ("What I saw today"). His smudged charcoal drawings, representing in various forms the majestic setting of the F/W 2012 menswear show-space, a "palace of role play" or "Il Palazzo", bear the charming imperfections that can only be left by human hands.
In fall 2012, Prada created some unique books, featuring Haines' original illustrations of the F/W 2012 menswear collection, drawn over the existing print-out, layering genres and eras to create random meanings and associations.
As a second stage of the project, Prada published a limited edition book, printed out in 500 copies only, featuring 150 original Haines artworks based on the Prada F/W 2012 menswear collection.
In the final chapter of the project, Prada launches a new app and a web section on Prada.com, allowing visitors to take an interactive tour inside the virtual Palazzo, created by James Lima.
Explore the rooms of the magnificent palace to discover a showcase of Prada accessories as well as Haines' artworks.
title: Il Palazzo
